title: Isocyanates in Paints, Glues, and Spray Foam
summary: Isocyanates in paints, glues, and spray foam can cause asthma and skin rashes. Once you are sensitized, even a small amount can trigger an attack.
talking_points: Isocyanates are in many construction products, including paints, glues, and spray polyurethane foam. Breathing the vapor or mist can cause asthma, and skin contact can cause a rash.
Some workers become sensitized. After that, even small amounts can cause an asthma attack or skin rash, and serious reactions can lead to disability or death.
Make sure the work area is ventilated and the ventilation equipment works.
Wear coveralls, chemical-resistant gloves, and eye protection.
Wear a supplied-air respirator when spraying indoors. Wear an air-purifying respirator with an organic vapor cartridge and P100 filter when spraying outside or working nearby.
Do not take your respirator off right after spraying.
If the product gets on your skin, wash right away with soap and water. Wash your hands before eating and drinking, and take off protective clothing before breaks and before going home.
Clean up the work area and store products properly. Ask for training. OSHA requires employers to train you, give you safety data sheets, and label products.
site_hazards_to_check: Spraying isocyanate products in an area with poor ventilation
Ventilation equipment that is off or not working
Workers without the right respirator, gloves, coveralls, or eye protection
Unlabeled products or no safety data sheet on site
Open containers or messy storage of coatings, glues, or foam
discussion_questions: Which products here contain isocyanates, and where are the safety data sheets?
